title: LLM token cadence tomography harness for burst vs steady-state TPS characterization
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build and maintain a tokens-per-second microbenchmark harness focused on 'tomography' — systematically characterizing LLM token throughput across burst, ramp, and steady-state regimes and producing p95 tail signals and automated regression alerts. This harness complements existing TPS suites by: (1) explicitly measuring short-duration bursts (100–300ms windows), (2) steady-state runs with realistic inter-request jitter, (3) KV-cache cold/warm transitions, and (4) model-normalized profiles so regressions are comparable across model sizes and quantization variants.
background: We have many TPS benchmarks (sustained throughput, microburst probes, etc.) but gaps remain in: fast-burst characterization, transition dynamics after KV cache invalidation, and a robust normalization layer to compare different model variants. Teams continue to be surprised by p95 regressions driven by cache-thrashing patterns or kernel selection changes. This ticket creates a focused harness and CI integration to catch these early.
proposed_solution: Create a modular harness that can run synthetic and trace-replay workloads against any model variant in the catalog. Key pieces: harness runner (go/python) with pluggable workload generators; a profiler that records tokens/sec, per-step latency histogram, kernel selection metadata, and KV cache hit/miss markers; normalization module to output tokens/sec relative to a model baseline; p95/regression detector that compares current run to baseline using configurable thresholds; CI job + datadog/dashboard + slack alerting for regressions. Provide documented run recipes for: burst-probe, steady-flow (50–300 concurrent simulated users), cache-warmup cycles, and mixed prompt-length distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute burst-probe, steady-flow, cache-cycle, and mixed-length scenarios against a target model with a single CLI command
Output includes tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, kernel-selection metadata, and KV cache hit/miss counts in JSON
Normalization step produces a model-relative TPS score and a human-readable report
Regression detector triggers a failure in CI if p95 or normalized-TPS deviates beyond configured thresholds
Dashboard with historical trend for tokens/sec and p95 is populated after first nightly run
Runbook documenting how to triage common failures (kernel regressions, cache thrash, infra noise) is checked in
success_metrics: Nightly runs for top-6 core models within 2 weeks
First CI regression alert triggered within 1 week of rollout (to validate path)
Reduction in silent p95 regressions (postmortem count) by 40% in next quarter
Mean time to detect throughput regression <= 6 hours after deployment
Dashboard adoption: at least 3 infra/serving engineers using the dashboard weekly
plan: Week 1: scaffold harness repo, CLI + workload generator, baseline runner for single model
Week 2: add KV-cache markers and cold/warm workflows, collect baseline runs for core models
Week 3: implement normalization layer and basic p95/regression detector; add JSON outputs
Week 4: wire CI job (nightly), push dashboard metrics and alerting, ship runbook
Week 5: iterate on false positives, extend to additional models and quantized variants
test_plan: Unit tests for workload generators and normalization code
Integration test running harness against a local dev model with synthetic traces
Canary CI runs against staging runtime to validate no noisy failures
Golden baseline comparison tests (store and compare) with tolerances
Manual verification: one full run with telemetry ends-to-end and dashboard population
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): run nightly for engineering-only models and validate alerts (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (expanded): include core production models and enable CI gating on a non-blocking channel (next 2 weeks)
Phase 3 (enforced): enable blocking CI failure for config-managed models after tuning thresholds
Communicate to runtime/compilation and serving teams; schedule 30-min sync to review first week results
open_risks: False positives from infra noise or transient GPU hotplug events can create alert fatigue
Normalization may mask real regressions if baselines are stale; requires regular baseline refresh
Telemetry overhead: collecting per-step histograms at high frequency might perturb performance; must validate sampling rate
CI runtime quotas: heavy nightly runs could spike Dedicated cost if not throttled
notes: We should reuse existing tokenization helpers from the tokenflow lib and model runners from serving-infra
Prefer lightweight Go runner for low overhead; Python harness wrappers allowed for orchestration and dashboards
Work with runtime team to surface kernel-selection tags in telemetry payloads
Consider adding an option to replay real production traces (sanitized) as a follow-up
